items.title: Harry "Sweets" Edison interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: I made the last CD of Billie Holiday called “Lady in Satin.” ... And we were very, very, very good friends.

ctx.x: And we are interested in hearing your stories and, of course where you got your nickname, we have to ask that, but—

Well when I first joined the Count Basie band in 1938, Lester Young, he was my roommate. And he had a knack for giving names to people that always stuck. So he gave me the name of “Sweets.” He gave Billie Holiday the name of “Lady Day,” and he named himself “Prez.”

items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: We had a manager named Maceo Birch, he travelled with the band, and Billie Holiday travelled with the band for a while when she first joined the band.

ctx.x: Do you remember some of the other groups you heard, bands you heard right on that first couple of days when you arrived?

Art Tatum…I walked up 7th Avenue and there was Ellington walking up the street and the next thing you know Claude Hopkins is walking up the street. Louis Armstrong, I’d see him on 7th Avenue. They’d all walk up and down 7th Avenue. Oh man, I said, gee, can you top this? I’m standing there just looking at them because most of the times I had seen them was on the stage and I’m out in the audience and here I am just about ready to shake his hand. Oh my goodness. After you get through work, you go up to Monroe’s…
Were you sitting in much or just listening?

items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: He named Billie Holiday 'Lady Day.' ... And then -- because after Billie Holiday left, we didn't want any singer anyway, you know. ... Billie Holiday made the best vocal on it, to me.

ctx.x: The main man, yes, the main man, you see. He named him Holy because he did the paying off, he was the bandleader. And he named me "Sweets." He named Billie Holiday "Lady Day." He named himself "Pres."
Oh, I thought Billie's supposed to have done that.
